IT 202.title: Computer Programming 1
IT 202.description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore significant real-world applications. In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the course integrates Marian Augustinian values in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute positively to society, embodying community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

clos.statement: Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.

 Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs, ensuring that solutions serve the common good, in line with Marian and Augustinian principles of truth and compassion. 

Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to develop Java- based programming solutions that address social challenges, demonstrating social responsibility and cultural sensitivity.
Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

IE-402.title: Systems Engineering
IE-402.description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis, design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students learn how to approach and solve large-scale engineering problems involving multiple components, stakeholders, and operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and performance evaluation. Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. Beyond technical knowledge, the course integrates Marian Augustinian values into each lesson, fostering the development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

clos.statement: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles by effectively leading and collaborating within teams, managing projects, and engaging in multidisciplinary environments.
Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information.
Develop the ability to identify and solve systems engineering challenges, making decisions that improve performance, enhance efficiency, and support sustainable practices across diverse industries.
Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

CpE 304.title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
CpE 304.description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on actuators are also included. Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

clos.statement: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions

Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

weekRow.assessment: Robust Design I – System Evaluation and Improvement Proposal Task: Have students apply basic robust design techniques to evaluate a system and propose design changes that would make it more stable under varying conditions. They should identify critical factors that affect performance and suggest improvements to minimize variability. Robust Design Report (I & II) Task: Students will submit a report for each part of the robust design application, detailing the steps taken to assess and improve system performance. For Robust Design I, they will focus on basic principles, and for Robust Design II, they will apply advanced techniques to optimize the system.
